newsitem.title: USA: Three U.S. drug firms post strong Q3 results. [CORRECTED 21:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Three U.S. drug firms post strong Q3 results. [CORRECTED 21:10 GMT]

text.p: Johnson and Johnson, Merck and Co Inc and Schering-Plough Corp on Wednesday beat Wall Street expectations with their third quarter earnings, using higher-margin new products to fight off the impact of a strong U.S. dollar.

The impact of the firm dollar, which trimmed about two percentage points off each company's sales by lowering foreign revenue in dollar terms, was offset by higher sales volume and cost savings, analysts said.
Whitehouse Station, N.J.-based Merck posted net income of $1.0 billion, or $0.83 a share. It was the first time Merck posted a billion dollars in quarterly profits.
The earnings per share were up from $0.70 a year ago and beat the First Call consensus estimate of $0.81.

Merck told industry analysts in a conference call that it was comfortable with estimates for its fourth quarter earnings in a range of $0.80 to $0.86 a share, but implied the bottom end of the range was too low. "The company's hitting on all cylinders, and the new products are doing very well," NatWest Securities analyst Jack Lamberton said.
Merck's biggest seller was the cholesterol-lowering drug Zocor, which had third quarter sales of $725 million, a 41 percent gain over 1995's third quarter.
Other new drugs, including the Cozaar and Hyzaar high blood pressure treatments and Fosamax for osteoporosis, also posted strong sales gains in the quarter, Merck said.

"I don't think people are going to be able to ignore these recently launched products," said Aros Securities analyst David Maris. Analysts noted that new drugs typically carry higher prices and heftier profit margins than older medications.
Shares in Merck, the largest U.S. drug company, were up 5/8 to 71-7/8 in afternoon trading.
New Brunswick, N.J.-based Johnson and Johnson posted third quarter net income of $750 million, or $0.56 a share, up from $0.48 a year ago and above Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.55.
(Corrects net income figure).

Its earnings were partly fueled by strong growth in the company's consumer product lines which were up 8.4 percent in the quarter over the year ago period, lead by the Tylenol and Neutrogena brands, analysts said.
It also got a boost from products from its recently acquired Cordis Corp and UltraCision units, they said.
"It was a very solid quarter and new product launches continue to drive growth," said Salomon Brothers analyst Eli Kammerman.
Johnson and Johnson was flat at 51-1/4 in late trading.
Madison, N.J.-based Schering-Plough reported third quarter net income of $291.7 million, or $0.79 a share, up from $0.68 a year ago and above the First Call consensus estimate of $0.78.

Third quarter worldwide sales of the non-sedating antihistamine Claritin line totaled $323 million, up 73 percent, while sales of the anti-cancer/anti-viral agent Intron A were $138 million, up 21 percent, the company said.
The sales of the drugs worked to offset declines in the Proventil inhaler asthma treatment, and for Eulexin, a prostate cancer drug, due to U.S. competition.

Some industry analysts have said Schering-Plough could have a tougher time in 1997 as Claritin faces growing compeitition from other allergy drugs including Hoechst AG's Allegra and Pfizer Inc's Zyrtec.
Schering was off one at 64.
--New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1733
